text: Validation performance of the k=16 five-field FM is materially sensitive to the precise training setup, with observed primary scores ranging from 0.6159 to 0.6384; the earlier 0.6282 result is therefore not a reliably reproduced expectation.

The particular 8-epoch SparseAdam run using user_id, video_id, author_id, tab, and duration_bucket scored 0.6159, but longer full-epoch training shows that this is not the ceiling of the same five-field k=16 FM family.

Using the exact five categorical fields with the native long_view label and multiple full training epochs allows a k=16 FM to reach primary 0.6384, exceeding the official 0.6016 baseline and both earlier reproduction attempts by more than seed noise.

Adding tag, upload_type, music_type, and hour to the five-field FM raises primary from 0.6384 to about 0.6568, with both GAUC and nDCG@5 improving; the bundled experiment does not identify which added field is responsible.

For the expanded FM, inverse-square-root user-frequency loss weighting lowers primary from 0.6568 to 0.6535 and nDCG@5 from 0.6258 to 0.6201 beyond seed noise, while the 0.0007 GAUC decrease is not measurable; this weighting should not replace the unweighted loss.

Augmenting the expanded FM with smoothed train-only user-context target-encoding residuals for tag, duration_bucket, upload_type, tab, music_type, and hour raises primary from 0.6568 to 0.6694; GAUC rises from 0.6877 to 0.6940 and nDCG@5 from 0.6258 to 0.6449.

Adding a sparse train-only user-author target-encoding residual to the context reranker produces no measurable gain: primary changes from 0.6694 to 0.6704 despite about 65.3% validation pair coverage, and later selection assigns the author residual a zero coefficient.

Under the tested pointwise binary-log-loss setup, categorical LightGBM alone consistently reaches primary about 0.6637, below the 0.6694 personalized FM/context reranker by about 0.0057, so it should not replace that reranker as a standalone model.

A 50% raw-score blend of pointwise categorical LightGBM with the personalized FM/context pipeline reaches primary 0.6730, improving over the 0.6694 personalized incumbent by 0.0036, with GAUC 0.6971 and nDCG@5 0.6490.

Splitting oversized user queries into contiguous subqueries of at most 8192 impressions avoids LightGBM's 10,000-row query limit and permits LambdaRank training, whereas leaving oversized queries unsplit crashes.

The tested split-query LambdaRank configuration is substantially worse than the pointwise categorical tree, with standalone primary 0.6260 versus 0.6637; blend selection gives it zero weight, and its resulting 0.6704 pipeline is 0.0026 below the best 0.6730 raw-score blend.

Vectorizing within-user score normalization and aggregation removes the per-user Python-loop bottleneck: the vectorized experiment completed in 670 seconds, whereas the loop-based version was killed at the 3000-second limit.

The tested vectorized user-conditional Gaussian/rank-normalized combination scores primary 0.6644 with 50% tree weight, 0.0086 below the 0.6730 raw-score blend, while nDCG@5 falls from 0.6490 to 0.6320; it should not replace raw-score blending.

With auxiliary click-loss weight 0.2, train-only long_view/is_click multi-task fine-tuning provides no measurable benefit: its best raw primary of 0.65625 is within noise of the same run's 0.65672 single-task FM, and the selected 30% tree blend scores 0.6730, identical in primary to the existing best pipeline.
